PLU1.claim: Ludhiana, founded in 1480 by the Lodhis on the Sutlej, is Punjab's most populous city — the 'Manchester of India' for its hosiery and woollens.

evidence.quote: Ludhiana was founded in 1480 as Lodhi-ana, named after the Lodhi dynasty that established it.

Situated on the banks of the Sutlej River, it is the most populous city in Punjab and has earned the title of the Manchester of India for its dominance in manufacturing and export of woollen garments, hosiery goods, cycle parts, machine components, sewing machines, and mopeds.

PLU2.claim: It is known for tandoori cooking in half-buried earthen ovens; the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics are held nearby every February, a tradition begun in 1933.

evidence.quote: Ludhiana is acclaimed for its Tandoori cuisine, cooked in huge earthen ovens buried half in the ground with a coal fire below.
The Kila Raipur Sports Festival, held annually near Ludhiana every February, is known as India's Rural Olympics.
It began in 1933 when philanthropist Inder Singh Grewal envisioned an annual gathering where farmers could test their physical endurance.

PLU3.claim: Ludhiana's Halwara airport serves the city, with Chandigarh and Amritsar the nearest international airports; Ludhiana Junction is a major Northern Railway junction; buses leave from the ISBT on the Grand Trunk Road; autos, shared vehicles and city buses run locally.

evidence.quote: How to Reach By Air: Ludhiana Airport (Halwara Airport) serves the city directly. Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (Mohali), and Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar, are the two international airports closest to Ludhiana.
By Train: Ludhiana Junction Railway Station is one of the major railway junctions on the Northern Railway network, with direct connections to Delhi, Amritsar, Chandigarh, and other major cities.

By Road: Ludhiana ISBT (Amar Shaheed Sukhdev Interstate Bus Terminal) is the main road transport hub, well connected by PRTC and private services to all major cities in Punjab and neighbouring states.
Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles, and city buses operate within Ludhiana city and between towns in the district.

PLU4.claim: Best October to March; February for Kila Raipur.

evidence.quote: February is the best time to attend the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics.

PLU6.claim: The district gave India the martyrs Kartar Singh Sarabha, Sukhdev Thapar and Lala Lajpat Rai; makki di roti with sarson da saag is the winter staple.

evidence.quote: Ludhiana district gave India three martyrs whose names are central to the story of Indian resistance to British rule: Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha, Shaheed Sukhdev Thapar, and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag is the winter staple found at dhabas and households across the district.

PLU5.claim: Punjab Tourism lists hotels including Radisson Blu, Hyatt Regency and Park Plaza, and several homestays.

evidence.quote: Hotels in the Area: Radisson Blu Hotel
Hyatt Regency

PJL1.claim: Jalandhar is believed to be Punjab's oldest city, between the Sutlej and Beas on the Grand Trunk Road; it was Punjab's capital after Partition and is now the largest city of the Doaba and a sports-goods hub.

evidence.quote: Jalandhar is believed to be the oldest city in Punjab, with its history stretching across Harappan, Vedic, Mauryan, Gupta, and Mughal periods.
A third account derives the name from the vernacular term meaning 'area inside the water', a reference to its position between the rivers Sutlej and Beas, alongside the historic Grand Trunk Road.
Jalandhar served as the capital of Punjab following the Partition of 1947 before the administrative headquarters shifted to Shimla and then to Chandigarh.
Today, Jalandhar is the largest city in the Doaba region and a hub of sports goods manufacturing, with products exported to countries across the world.

PJL2.claim: Devi Talab Mandir is one of the 51 Shakti Pithas and hosts the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan each December, India's oldest Hindustani classical music festival; nearby Sansarpur is the 'nursery of hockey players'.

evidence.quote: Devi Talab Mandir is one of India's 51 Shakti Pithas. In Jalandhar, the presiding goddess is known as Tripurmalini, and the right breast of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen at this site.
The Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan, held annually in December at Devi Talab Mandir, is the oldest Hindustani classical music festival in the country.

The village of Sansarpur, in the vicinity of Jalandhar Cantonment, is known as the Nursery of Hockey Players and has produced multiple Olympians including Balbir Singh, Gurdev Singh, Tarsem Singh, Harbinder Singh, and Ajit Pal Singh.

PJL3.claim: Adampur airport is about 25 km away and Amritsar about 75 km; buses run from the city bus stand on NH 1; autos and local buses get around town. Best October to March.

evidence.quote: A domestic airport is located at Adampur, Jalandhar, approximately 25 km from Jalandhar Bus Stand and 23 km from Jalandhar City Railway Station.
The second nearest airport is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar, approximately 75 km northwest of Jalandhar.
By Road: Jalandhar City Bus Stand is the main road transport hub, with regular PRTC and private services connecting Jalandhar to major cities across Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Delhi.
Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles, and local buses operate within Jalandhar city and between towns in the district.

PJL4.claim: Local staples include makki di roti with sarson da saag, chole bhature, Amritsari kulcha and Jalandhari fish fry. Punjab Tourism lists Sarovar Portico, Ramada Encore, Golden Tulip and Radisson.

evidence.quote: Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag, Chole Bhature, Amritsari Kulcha, Dal Makhani, and Patiala Lassi are among the staples widely available across the city.
Jalandhari Fish Fry and Butter Chicken represent the city's non-vegetarian tradition.
Hotels in the Area: Sarovar Portico Jalandhar, Ramada Encore by Wyndham Jalandhar, Golden Tulip Jalandhar, Radisson Hotel Jalandhar
Best Time to Visit: October to March

PJL5.claim: Nurmahal, with its Mughal serai, is 33 km from Jalandhar.

evidence.quote: Nurmahal, located 33 km from Jalandhar, is a town steeped in history and Mughal architecture.

PBT1.claim: Bathinda, in the Malwa, is one of Punjab's oldest cities and is called the City of Lakes for its five artificial lakes.

evidence.quote: Bathinda district lies in the Malwa region of Punjab. It is bounded by Faridkot and Moga in the north, Muktsar in the west, Barnala and Mansa in the east, and the state of Haryana in the south.

Bathinda is popularly known as the City of Lakes on account of its five artificial lakes. Takht Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo is one of the five Takhts the highest seats of temporal authority in Sikhism.
History & Background Bathinda is one of the oldest cities in Punjab. According to historical records cited in the Ainai-Barar Bans , the city was founded by Bhati Rao in the third century.
The land is a flat agricultural belt, historically part of the Lakhi Jungle region, and the district is a significant cotton and wheat producing zone.

PBT2.claim: Qila Mubarak, an ASI monument standing since the 12th century, is among India's oldest surviving forts; Razia Sultana was imprisoned there.

evidence.quote: The fort, which has stood since the 12th century, is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and has been declared the oldest surviving fort in India.
It is the site where Malik Ikhtiar-ud-din Altunia, the 13th-century Governor of Bathinda, rebelled and imprisoned Empress Razia Sultana, one of the most powerful rulers of the Delhi Sultanate.
Famously, the governor and the empress fell in love during her captivity, and went on to marry each other.

Razia Sultana , the first woman ruler of India, was imprisoned in Qila Mubarak in 1240 AD. The district is home to prestigious institutions including the Central University of Punjab , Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Technical University , and AIIMS Bathinda .

PBT3.claim: Bathinda airport is about 25 km away with flights to Delhi and Jammu; Bathinda Junction has trains to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and more; buses run from the bus stand; autos and tempos get around.

evidence.quote: How to Reach By Air: Bathinda has its own domestic airport located approximately 25–26 km from the city, with flights connecting to New Delhi and Jammu.
By Rail: Bathinda Junction is one of the major railway junctions in northern Punjab, situated on the Ambala–Bathinda branch line.
PRTC and PUNBUS services operate from Bathinda Bus Stand to cities across Punjab and neighbouring states.
Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos operate within Bathinda city and between the city and nearby attractions.

PBT4.claim: Best October to March; summers exceed 40 °C. Food is Malwa home and dhaba cooking in desi ghee.

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit: October to March.
Summers (April–June) are hot, often above 40°C.
Food & Flavours The food of Bathinda is the food of the Malwa heartland cooked in desi ghee, built on dairy, and heavy with the flavours of wheat and mustard.

PPK1.claim: Pathankot, where Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir meet, lies in the Shivalik foothills between the Ravi and Chakki rivers at about 332 m, and is the gateway to Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Kangra and Chamba.

evidence.quote: Pathankot is situated in the northernmost part of Punjab, where the states of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir converge.

Nestled in the foothills of the Shivalik Range and surrounded by the Ravi and Chakki rivers, the district serves as the gateway to the Himalayan hill destinations of Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Kangra, and Chamba.
With an average elevation of 332 metres and views of the snow-capped Himalayas to the north, the district is characterised by lush greenery, river valleys, and forested foothills.
Owing to its strategic location, Pathankot has historically been an important centre for travel, trade, and cultural exchange between the plains and the hills.

PPK2.claim: It is known for litchis exported abroad, the Shahpurkandi Fort, the Ranjit Sagar Dam on the Ravi and the Atal Setu bridge.

evidence.quote: Pathankot is famous for its high-quality litchi production and exports its produce to countries including the UAE, France, Canada, Thailand, and Saudi Arabia.
The district is home to the historic Shahpurkandi Fort and is closely associated with the princely state of Nurpur.

Places to Visit Ranjit Sagar Dam Located near Shahpurkandi, Ranjit Sagar Dam is one of the largest hydroelectric projects in Northern India. Built on the Ravi River, the dam is surrounded by forested hills and offers panoramic views of the reservoir and the surrounding landscape.
The modern Atal Setu bridge has emerged as one of Punjab's most photographed tourism landmarks.

PPK3.claim: Pathankot airport, 3 km from the centre, has flights to Delhi; Pathankot Junction and Cantonment stations link Delhi, Jammu, Amritsar and beyond; roads lead to Amritsar (110 km), Jammu (105 km), Dharamshala (85 km) and Dalhousie (80 km).

evidence.quote: How to Reach By Air Pathankot is served by Pathankot Airport (IXP) , a domestic airport located approximately 3 km from the city centre and about 7 km from Pathankot Railway Station .

The airport operates flights connecting Pathankot with Delhi. For international and wider domestic connectivity, the nearest international airport is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar , located approximately 119 km away .
Pathankot Cantonment Railway Station and Pathankot Junction connect the district with Delhi, Amritsar, Jammu, Chandigarh, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Kolkata, and other major cities.
The district is connected by National Highways to major cities including Amritsar (110 km), Jammu (105 km), Dharamshala (85 km), Dalhousie (80 km), Kangra (95 km), and Chandigarh (250 km).

PPK4.claim: Best October to March, especially spring (February–April).

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit: October to March.
Spring (February–April) is especially enjoyable, while summers can be hot and monsoons receive moderate to heavy rainfall.

PTT1.claim: Tarn Taran was founded in 1596 by Guru Arjan Dev Ji; its Sri Darbar Sahib has the largest sarovar of any gurdwara and is considered a replica of the Harmandir Sahib.

evidence.quote: History & Background Tarn Taran was founded in 1596 by Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru.

The Gurudwara holds a unique distinction among all Sikh shrines: it is home to the largest Sarovar (holy water tank) of any Gurudwara in the world, and is the only Gurudwara considered a replica of the revered Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar.

The Gurudwara holds a unique distinction among all Sikh shrines: it is home to the largest Sarovar (holy water tank) of any Gurudwara in the world, and is the only Gurudwara considered a replica of the revered Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar.

PTT2.claim: The name means 'the boat that takes one across the ocean of existence'; the sarovar was known as Dukh Nivaran.

evidence.quote: the full phrase means "the boat that takes one across the ocean of existence."
For this reason, the Sarovar has historically been known as Dukh Nivaran — the eradicator of affliction.

PTT3.claim: Amritsar airport is about 25 km away; Tarn Taran station is on the Amritsar–Ferozepur line; buses run from Amritsar; autos and tempos get around. Harike Wetland is in the district.

evidence.quote: How to Reach By Air: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (IATA: ATQ) — approximately 25 km from Tarn Taran Sahib.
By Train: Tarn Taran has its own railway station on the Amritsar–Ferozepur line. Amritsar Junction, approximately 25 km away, is the nearest major railhead with broader national connectivity.
By Road: Regular PRTC and PUNBUS services run from Amritsar Bus Stand to Tarn Taran. The district connects Amritsar with the cities of the Majha region.
Harike Wetland, located in this district, is the largest wetland in northern India and is a designated Ramsar site.

PTT4.claim: Best October to March; the Amavasya pilgrimage takes place every month.

evidence.quote: Amavasya pilgrimage is active every month throughout the year.
Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos operate within Tarn Taran town and between towns in the district.

PAS1.claim: Anandpur Sahib, on the Sutlej about 40 km from Rupnagar, was founded by Guru Teg Bahadur and is the birthplace of the Khalsa, created by Guru Gobind Singh on Baisakhi 1699.

evidence.quote: Anandpur Sahib, located on the left bank of the Sutlej approximately 40 km from Rupnagar town, was founded by Sri Guru Teg Bahadur Ji and is the birthplace of the Khalsa.
It was here that Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa on Baisakhi Day in 1699, the most significant event in the history of the Sikh faith.

PAS2.claim: Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, the principal shrine, keeps Guru Gobind Singh's weapons; Anandgarh Fort, begun in 1689, was one of five forts he built.

evidence.quote: Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib is the principal shrine of Anandpur Sahib. This is a historic site where, on the day of Baisakhi in 1699, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated his followers into the order of the Khalsa.
In the sanctum sanctorum of Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, a number of the belongings of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji are preserved- a khanda, a dagger, a shield, a chakkar, three swords and several spears.
Anandgarh Fort is one of the five forts built by Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji to protect Sikhs and other residents from the Mughal Empire.
It is believed that the construction of this fort began in 1689 and took over a decade to complete.

PAS5.claim: October to March is the most comfortable season.

evidence.quote: October to March is the most comfortable season.

PAS3.claim: Hola Mohalla (February/March) and Baisakhi (April) are the main times to visit; langar runs round the clock at Takht Keshgarh Sahib.

evidence.quote: Hola Mohalla in February/March and Baisakhi in April are the most significant times to visit Anandpur Sahib.

At the Gurdwaras of Anandpur Sahib, particularly at Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, round-the-clock langar is served free to all visitors regardless of faith or background during Hola Mohalla, this langar is extended along the roads leading into the city from all directions.

PAS4.claim: Chandigarh airport is the nearest; Anandpur Sahib has its own station; buses run from Chandigarh and other cities.

evidence.quote: How to Reach By Air: The nearest airport is Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (Mohali). Rupnagar is approximately 50 km from Chandigarh.
Anandpur Sahib Railway Station serves the Anandpur Sahib area directly. By Road: Regular bus services operate from Chandigarh and other major cities in Punjab to Rupnagar and Anandpur Sahib.
By Road: Regular bus services operate from Chandigarh and other major cities in Punjab to Rupnagar and Anandpur Sahib. Rupnagar is approximately 50 km from Chandigarh.

PAS2B.claim: Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, the principal shrine, keeps Guru Gobind Singh's weapons; Anandgarh Fort, begun in 1689, was one of five forts he built.

evidence.quote: Here, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji baptized five brave men with amrit (holy water).

PDS1.claim: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, one of the five Takhts, is at Talwandi Sabo, 28 km from Bathinda; Guru Gobind Singh rested here for nearly a year and compiled the final version of the Guru Granth Sahib in 1705.

evidence.quote: One of the five sacred Takhts of Sikhism, Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is a gleaming white Gurudwara located in Talwandi Sabo (28 km from Bathinda).
It is the place where the tenth Sikh Guru, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, took rest for nearly a year and compiled the final version of the holy Sikh scripture 'Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji' in the year 1705.
Takht Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo is one of the five Takhts the highest seats of temporal authority in Sikhism.

After his fiercest battles with the Mughals at Anandpur Sahib, Chamkaur Sahib, and Muktsar, Guru Gobind Singh Ji retired to the jungles of Malwa and took rest ( Dam ) at Talwandi Sabo hence the name Damdama Sahib.

PDS2.claim: The Guru's sword, seal and mirror are kept here, and more relics are shown at Gurdwara Daleh di Kothi nearby; it is called Guru ki Kashi.

evidence.quote: Large numbers of devotees visit this place to seek blessings and witness the belongings of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, which include a sword, seal and a sacred mirror, stored in the premises of the Gurudwara.
Just 10 minutes away from Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
Places to Visit Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo One of the five Takhts of Sikhism and known as Guru Ki Kashi the Banaras of the Guru.

PDS3.claim: The Baisakhi Mela in April is the biggest festival.

evidence.quote: The Baisakhi Mela at Damdama Sahib (April)

PDU1.claim: Durgiana Temple, also called the Laxmi Narayan Temple, stands in the middle of a sarovar about 1.5 km from the Golden Temple, reached by a bridge; its tank measures 541 ft by 432 ft.

evidence.quote: Situated in the middle of the sarover Shri Durgiana Temple is an important and world-renowned religious place for the Hindus in the holy city of Amritsar in the Punjab province of northern India, where thousands of devotees come daily to worship and pay obeisance.
The bridge provides an approach to the temple. The temple tank is 541 ft X 432 ft and 20 ft deep, which according to government records was built here in 16th century.
The temple tank is 541 ft X 432 ft and 20 ft deep, which according to government records was built here in 16th century.
Located roughly at a distance of about one and a half kilometers from the Golden Temple, Durgiana Temple is dedicated to the Hindu Goddess and is also known as the Laxmi Narayan Temple.

PDU2.claim: Its domes are covered in gold and its entrance has a 12 ft silver door; Lakshmi-Narayan, Ram Darbar and Radha-Krishna are enshrined. Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya laid the foundation stone in 1924.

evidence.quote: Domes of the main temple along with the upper side of the walls adjacent to it are carved with Gold.
12X12 feet huge silver carved and engraved door

In the central GARBH GRAH inside the main temple idols of Shri Lakshmi-Narayan in the standng position and on one side of them Shri Ram Darbar and on the other side the idols of Shri Radha-Krishna Ji along with Shri Giriraj Ji Maharaj present a wonderful divine look.
The foundation stone of Shri Durgiana Temple was laid by Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya in 1924 on the day of Ganga Dashami (Dussehra).

PDU3.claim: It is half a kilometre from the railway station and 1.5 km from the bus stand, near Lohgarh Gate; Ram Tirath, linked to Valmiki, is about 8 km away.

evidence.quote: It is just half a kilometer away from the railway station and about 1.5 km from the bus stand.
His sons Luv and Kush spent their child-hood with their mother Sita in the ashram of Maharshi Valmiki, Ram Tirtha, which is about 8 km from the temple.

PMM1.claim: Kapurthala's rose-hued Moorish Mosque, with a blue-tiled roof, was built in the 1930s to designs by the French architect M. Manteaux; artists from the Mayo School of Art, Lahore, decorated its dome. It is an ASI national monument.

evidence.quote: the French inspired rose-hued mosque with a blue tiled roof known as the 'Moorish Mosque' was built in the 1930s.

A visit to Kapurthala is incomplete without seeing this masterpiece designed by French architect M Manteaux, with a dome richly decorated inside by a team of artists from the Mayo School of Art, Lahore.
The mosque is listed as a National Monument by the Archaeological Survey of India
It serves as a great example of the secular traditions of Punjab.

PMM2.claim: Kapurthala is about 20 km from Jalandhar; its Jagatjit Palace (1908) is modelled on Versailles.

evidence.quote: The district is approximately 20 km from Jalandhar, 75 km from Amritsar, 165 km from Chandigarh, and around 40 km from Sultanpur Lodhi.
Built in 1908 by Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, the palace is modelled on the Palace of Versailles in France and showcases remarkable Indo-Saracenic architecture.

PHW1.claim: The Hussainiwala National Martyrs Memorial (1968) marks where Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were cremated on 23 March 1931; a Shaheedi Mela is held every 23 March and the BSF holds a daily retreat ceremony.

evidence.quote: Built in 1968, the Hussainiwala National Martyrs Memorial is a tribute to revolutionary heroes Shaheed Bhagat Singh, Shaheed Rajguru and Shaheed Sukhdev who were cremated there on 23rd March 1931.
A 'Shaheedi Mela' (Martyr's fair) takes place on 23rd March every year to commemorate the martyrdom of these freedom fighters.

Tourists from all corners of the world visit this well-maintained park to see the life-sized black granite statues of the three brave martyrs, standing in a pose evoking their famous slogan – “Inquilab Zindabad”.
A daily retreat ceremony reminiscent of the Attari-Wagah border ceremony is also held here by the Border Security Forc.

PKC1.claim: The Kartarpur Sahib Corridor lets Indian pilgrims visit Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib in Narowal district, Pakistan, where Guru Nanak spent his last eighteen years and died on 22 September 1539.

evidence.quote: Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor which serves as vital spiritual and cultural link allowing pilgrims from India to visit Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib is situated in Narowal District of Western Punjab, Pakistan.
Sri Kartarpur Sahib is associated with the last eighteen years of Guru Nanak Devji where he left for heavenly abode on September 22, 1539.

PKC2.claim: Kartarpur went to Pakistan under the Radcliffe Award of 17 August 1947; the corridor starts at Dera Baba Nanak, about 40 km from Gurdaspur, 35 km from Batala and 48 km from Amritsar.

evidence.quote: Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib situated in Shakargarh Tehsil of District Gurdaspur became part of Pakistan as a result of Sir Cyril Radcliffe Award announced on August 17, 1947 which partitioned the District in two parts and awarded Shakargarh Tehsil to Pakistan.
The town of Dera Baba Nanak is situated at a distance of about 40 kms from the District Head quarters town of Gurdaspur.
A number of roads connect this historic town with Batala (35 km) and Amritsar (48 km). National Highway No 503 D will connect it with Jalandhar Amritsar road via Batala and Chowk Mehta.

PKC3.claim: The present Darbar Sahib buildings at Kartarpur date from 1911–12.

evidence.quote: The present building of Darbar Sahib Shrine at Kartarpur Sahib and residential quarters were constructed in 1911-1912. It has a symbolic platform raised in the memory of Sri Guru Nanak Devji's final resting place.

PNM1.claim: Nurmahal, 33 km from Jalandhar, grew around a Mughal caravanserai built in 1618 under Zakariya Khan on the order of Nur Jahan, on the Lahore–Agra route.

evidence.quote: Nurmahal, located 33 km from Jalandhar, is a town steeped in history and Mughal architecture.
The town derives its name from Nur Jahan, the wife of Emperor Jahangir, who is believed to have been brought up here.

Built under the supervision of Zakariya Khan, the then Governor of Doab (the region of Punjab) in 1618, the serai was intended to provide a safe and comfortable stop for travellers and traders on the Lahore-Agra route.

PNM2.claim: The quadrangular serai has 140 cells around a courtyard; its red sandstone Western Gateway is carved with birds, elephants, camels, fairies and humans, with verse inscriptions at the entrance.

evidence.quote: The serai, in the form of a quadrangle consisting of 140 cells, is built around a large courtyard, typical of the caravanserais used during the Mughal period, which were designed to accommodate people, goods, and animals.
The majestic Western Gateway is made of red sandstone, and has intricate carvings depicting birds, elephants, camels, fairies and humans.
At the entrance to the gateway, there are inscriptions written in four rhyming verses, flanked by scenes of fighting animals and sculpted lotus mounds.

places.name: Ludhiana
places.summary: Punjab's biggest city — hosiery bazaars, tandoori kitchens and the February Rural Olympics at Kila Raipur.
places.seoTitle: Ludhiana: Tandoori Food, Kila Raipur Rural Olympics, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Ludhiana, Punjab's largest city on the Sutlej: the 'Manchester of India', famous tandoori food and the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics each February; how to get there.

overview.text: Ludhiana was founded in 1480 as Lodhi-ana, named after the Lodhi dynasty, and stands on the Sutlej. It is Punjab's most populous city and earned the name 'Manchester of India' for its mills, hosiery, woollens, cycle parts and machine tools, which are sold around the world. For visitors Ludhiana is above all a food city, celebrated for tandoori cooking done in big earthen ovens half-buried in the ground over coal. Every February the nearby village of Kila Raipur hosts the Rural Olympics, begun in 1933 so that farmers could test their strength and endurance. Ludhiana is also the home district of the freedom fighters Kartar Singh Sarabha, Sukhdev Thapar and Lala Lajpat Rai.

best_time.text: October to March. Come in February for the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics.

how_to_reach.text: Halwara airport serves Ludhiana directly; the nearest international airports are Chandigarh (Mohali) and Amritsar. Ludhiana Junction is one of the main junctions of the Northern Railway, and the city sits on the Grand Trunk Road with buses from the ISBT across Punjab and beyond.

local_transport.text: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles and city buses run within the city and to nearby towns.

items.body: Makki di roti with sarson da saag in winter.

where_to_stay.text: Punjab Tourism lists hotels such as Radisson Blu, Hyatt Regency and Park Plaza, plus several homestays.

items.body: See the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics in February.

places.seoTitle: Jalandhar: Devi Talab Mandir, Harballabh Festival, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Jalandhar between the Sutlej and Beas: Devi Talab Mandir (a Shakti Pitha), the December Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan, Nurmahal Serai nearby; Adampur airport 25 km.

overview.text: Jalandhar is believed to be the oldest city in Punjab, its story running through Harappan, Vedic, Mauryan, Gupta and Mughal times. It lies between the Sutlej and the Beas on the Grand Trunk Road, and after Partition in 1947 it briefly served as Punjab's capital. Today it is the largest city of the Doaba region and a centre of sports-goods manufacturing. Its spiritual heart is the Devi Talab Mandir, one of the 51 Shakti Pithas, which every December hosts the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan, India's oldest festival of Hindustani classical music. Nearby Sansarpur is known as the nursery of hockey players, and the Mughal serai at Nurmahal is a short drive away.

best_time.text: October to March; December for the Harballabh music festival.

how_to_reach.text: Adampur domestic airport is about 25 km from the bus stand; Amritsar international airport is about 75 km away. Buses run from Jalandhar City Bus Stand across Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Delhi; the city lies on NH 1.

local_transport.text: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles and local buses.

places.name: Bathinda
places.summary: The Malwa's 'City of Lakes', with Qila Mubarak — one of India's oldest forts — and Damdama Sahib nearby.
places.seoTitle: Bathinda: Qila Mubarak, City of Lakes and Damdama Sahib
places.seoDescription: Bathinda in Punjab's Malwa: Qila Mubarak, a 12th-century fort where Razia Sultana was held; five lakes; Takht Damdama Sahib 28 km away; best October–March.

overview.text: Bathinda is one of the oldest cities in Punjab and the chief town of the Malwa region, a flat belt of wheat and cotton country. Its nickname, the City of Lakes, comes from its five artificial lakes. At its centre stands Qila Mubarak, an ASI-protected fort that has stood since the 12th century and is counted among the oldest surviving forts in India. It is remembered for a romance: in 1240 Empress Razia Sultana was imprisoned here by Malik Altunia, Bathinda's governor, and the two later married. About 28 km away at Talwandi Sabo is Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, one of the five Takhts of Sikhism. October to March is the time to come; summers top 40 °C.

items.title: Airport
items.body: About 25 km; flights to Delhi and Jammu

best_time.text: October to March. Summers, April to June, are often above 40 °C.

how_to_reach.text: Bathinda's domestic airport, about 25 km out, has flights to New Delhi and Jammu. Bathinda Junction is a major junction with trains to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and other cities. PRTC and PUNBUS buses run from the bus stand across Punjab and beyond.

local_transport.text: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos run in the city and to nearby sights.

places.name: Pathankot
places.summary: Punjab's gateway to the Himalaya, where three states meet below the Shivaliks.
places.seoTitle: Pathankot: Gateway to Dalhousie and Dharamshala, How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Pathankot, where Punjab, Himachal and J&K meet: Ranjit Sagar Dam, Shahpurkandi Fort, litchis; airport with Delhi flights, rail junction; 80 km to Dalhousie.

overview.text: Pathankot sits in the northernmost corner of Punjab, the only district where Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir meet. Set at about 332 m in the Shivalik foothills between the Ravi and Chakki rivers, with snow peaks visible to the north, it has long been the link between the plains and the hills, and today it is the gateway to Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Kangra and Chamba. Around it are the Ranjit Sagar Dam on the Ravi, one of north India's largest hydroelectric projects, the historic Shahpurkandi Fort and the much-photographed Atal Setu bridge. Pathankot is also known for its litchis, exported as far as the UAE, France and Canada.

best_time.text: October to March; spring, February to April, is especially pleasant.

how_to_reach.text: Pathankot airport, 3 km from the centre, has flights to Delhi; Amritsar is the nearest international airport. Pathankot Junction and Cantonment stations link Delhi, Amritsar, Jammu, Chandigarh and beyond. By road it is about 110 km from Amritsar, 105 km from Jammu, 85 km from Dharamshala and 80 km from Dalhousie.

places.name: Tarn Taran
places.summary: Guru Arjan Dev's 1596 town, with the largest sarovar of any gurdwara — 25 km from Amritsar.
places.seoTitle: Tarn Taran Sahib: Gurdwara, Sarovar and How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Tarn Taran, founded by Guru Arjan Dev in 1596: Sri Darbar Sahib with the largest gurdwara sarovar, the monthly Amavasya pilgrimage, 25 km from Amritsar airport.

overview.text: Tarn Taran was founded in 1596 by Guru Arjan Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru, who began the great sarovar and its gurdwara here. Sri Darbar Sahib has the largest sarovar of any gurdwara in the world and is the only one considered a replica of the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. The name, given first to the tank, means 'the boat that takes one across the ocean of existence', and the water — once believed to cure leprosy — was known as Dukh Nivaran, the eradicator of affliction. The town is 25 km from Amritsar, and the Amavasya pilgrimage brings devotees every month. Harike Wetland, a Ramsar site, also lies in the district.

best_time.text: October to March. The Amavasya pilgrimage takes place every month.

how_to_reach.text: Amritsar's international airport is about 25 km away. Tarn Taran station is on the Amritsar–Ferozepur line, and PRTC and PUNBUS buses run from Amritsar bus stand.

local_transport.text: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos run in the town.

places.name: Anandpur Sahib
places.summary: The birthplace of the Khalsa on the Sutlej — Takht Keshgarh Sahib and the Hola Mohalla festival.
places.seoTitle: Anandpur Sahib: Takht Keshgarh Sahib, Hola Mohalla, How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Anandpur Sahib on the Sutlej, where Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa in 1699: Takht Keshgarh Sahib, Anandgarh Fort, Hola Mohalla and Baisakhi.

overview.text: Anandpur Sahib lies on the left bank of the Sutlej, about 40 km from Rupnagar. Founded by Guru Teg Bahadur, it is the birthplace of the Khalsa: here, on Baisakhi Day in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh initiated the first five Sikhs with amrit. Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, the town's principal shrine, marks the spot and preserves weapons that belonged to the Guru — a khanda, a dagger, a shield, swords and spears. Anandgarh Fort, one of five forts he built to protect the town, was begun in 1689. The town is busiest at Hola Mohalla in February or March and at Baisakhi in April, and langar is served round the clock.

best_time.text: Any time; October to March is the most comfortable. Hola Mohalla (February/March) and Baisakhi (April) are the great festivals.

how_to_reach.text: Chandigarh (Mohali) is the nearest airport. Anandpur Sahib has its own railway station, and buses run from Chandigarh and other Punjab cities.

items.title: What happened at Anandpur Sahib in 1699?
items.body: Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa on Baisakhi Day.

places.name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
places.summary: One of Sikhism's five Takhts at Talwandi Sabo, where the Guru Granth Sahib was completed in 1705.
places.seoTitle: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo: History and Visiting
places.seoDescription: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo, 28 km from Bathinda: one of the five Takhts, where Guru Gobind Singh completed the Guru Granth Sahib in 1705.

overview.text: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is a gleaming white gurdwara at Talwandi Sabo, 28 km from Bathinda, and one of the five Takhts, the highest seats of authority in Sikhism. After his battles with the Mughals, Guru Gobind Singh rested here for nearly a year and in 1705 compiled the final version of the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib — which is why Talwandi Sabo is called Guru ki Kashi, the Guru's Banaras. Devotees come to see the Guru's belongings kept here, including a sword, a seal and a sacred mirror, and ten minutes away more of his weapons and garments are displayed at Gurdwara Daleh di Kothi. The Baisakhi Mela in April draws the largest crowds.

places.name: Durgiana Temple
places.summary: Amritsar's great Hindu temple, set in its own sarovar 1.5 km from the Golden Temple.
places.seoTitle: Durgiana Temple, Amritsar: Silver Doors, Sarovar and Location
places.seoDescription: Durgiana (Laxmi Narayan) Temple in Amritsar: a gold-domed temple in a sarovar, with 12 ft silver doors, half a kilometre from the railway station.

overview.text: Durgiana Temple, also known as the Laxmi Narayan Temple, is Amritsar's most important Hindu shrine, standing in the middle of its own sarovar about one and a half kilometres from the Golden Temple. A bridge leads across the 541 ft by 432 ft tank to the temple, whose domes and upper walls are covered in gold. The main entrance has a huge 12 ft silver door, carved and engraved, and inside the sanctum stand Lakshmi-Narayan, with Ram Darbar on one side and Radha-Krishna on the other. Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya laid the foundation stone of the present temple in 1924. It is half a kilometre from the railway station, and Ram Tirath, linked to the sage Valmiki, is about 8 km away.

items.title: Location
items.body: Near Lohgarh Gate; 0.5 km from the railway station, 1.5 km from the bus stand

places.name: Moorish Mosque
places.summary: Kapurthala's 1930s rose-coloured mosque in Moroccan style, designed by a French architect.
places.seoTitle: Moorish Mosque, Kapurthala: History and Design
places.seoDescription: The Moorish Mosque in Kapurthala: a rose-hued, blue-roofed mosque of the 1930s by French architect M. Manteaux, with a dome painted by Mayo School artists.

overview.text: The Moorish Mosque is Kapurthala's most unusual monument. Built in the 1930s, the rose-coloured mosque with its blue-tiled roof was designed by the French architect M. Manteaux in a Moorish style. The inside of its dome was richly decorated by a team of artists from the Mayo School of Art in Lahore. Punjab Tourism presents it as a fine example of the state's secular traditions, and it is protected as a national monument by the Archaeological Survey of India. Kapurthala is about 20 km from Jalandhar, so the mosque pairs easily with the town's other landmark, the Jagatjit Palace, which Maharaja Jagatjit Singh built in 1908 on the model of Versailles.

places.name: Hussainiwala Border and Martyrs Memorial
places.summary: The memorial to Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev on the border near Ferozepur, with a daily retreat ceremony.
places.seoTitle: Hussainiwala Border: Martyrs Memorial and Retreat Ceremony
places.seoDescription: Hussainiwala near Ferozepur: the 1968 memorial where Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were cremated, the 23 March Shaheedi Mela and a daily BSF retreat.

overview.text: Hussainiwala, on the border near Ferozepur, is where the revolutionaries Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were cremated on 23 March 1931. The National Martyrs Memorial, built in 1968, honours them with life-sized black granite statues of the three men, posed as if calling their famous slogan, 'Inquilab Zindabad'. Every year on 23 March a Shaheedi Mela, or martyrs' fair, commemorates their martyrdom, and visitors come from far and wide to the well-kept memorial park. The Border Security Force also holds a daily retreat ceremony here, reminiscent of the better-known Attari-Wagah ceremony near Amritsar, which makes an evening visit worthwhile.

items.body: Life-sized black granite statues of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev in the memorial park

places.name: Kartarpur Sahib Corridor (Dera Baba Nanak)
places.summary: The corridor from Dera Baba Nanak to Gurdwara Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan, where Guru Nanak spent his final years.
places.seoTitle: Kartarpur Sahib Corridor: Dera Baba Nanak, History, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Kartarpur Sahib Corridor from Dera Baba Nanak, 48 km from Amritsar: the link to Gurdwara Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan, where Guru Nanak spent his last 18 years.

overview.text: The Kartarpur Sahib Corridor links Dera Baba Nanak, in Punjab's Gurdaspur district, with Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib in Narowal district, Pakistan. Kartarpur is where Guru Nanak spent the last eighteen years of his life and died on 22 September 1539, and a raised platform marks his final resting place; the present shrine buildings date from 1911–12. When the Radcliffe Award of 17 August 1947 divided Gurdaspur district, Kartarpur fell on the Pakistani side, only a few kilometres from the border, and Sikhs campaigned for decades for a passage to it. The corridor starts at Dera Baba Nanak, about 40 km from Gurdaspur, 35 km from Batala and 48 km from Amritsar.

items.title: Distances
items.body: Amritsar 48 km; Batala 35 km; Gurdaspur 40 km

places.name: Nurmahal Serai
places.summary: A 1618 Mughal caravanserai built for Nur Jahan, with a richly carved red sandstone gateway.
places.seoTitle: Nurmahal Serai: Mughal Caravanserai near Jalandhar
places.seoDescription: Nurmahal Serai, 33 km from Jalandhar: a 1618 Mughal caravanserai on the Lahore–Agra route built for Nur Jahan, with 140 cells and a carved sandstone gate.

overview.text: Nurmahal, 33 km from Jalandhar, is a small town built around one of Punjab's finest Mughal monuments. It takes its name from Nur Jahan, Emperor Jahangir's wife, who is believed to have grown up here, and on her orders a caravanserai was built in 1618 under Zakariya Khan, governor of the Doab, as a safe stop for travellers and traders on the Lahore–Agra road. The serai is a quadrangle of 140 cells around a large courtyard. Its majestic Western Gateway, of red sandstone, is carved with birds, elephants, camels, fairies and human figures, and verses inscribed at the entrance are flanked by fighting animals and lotus mounds.

items.title: Built
items.body: 1618, under Zakariya Khan, for travellers on the Lahore–Agra road

items.title: Look for
items.body: The red sandstone Western Gateway, carved with birds, elephants, camels and fairies, and its four rhyming verses
